assessments.reasoning: The FSF's complete 1.3 §10 at [19211,20299) states the designation, public acceptance and permanent choice requirements together. Its adjacent version-selection clauses explain how a licensee could independently have a choice even when the proxy conditions fail.

limitations: A particular election requires evidence of the work's authorized terms and the designated proxy's actual public statement covering the version. An illustrative Addendum or catalog identifier establishes neither fact.
reasoning: Under 1.3 §10, the Document must give a proxy authority to decide which future versions may be used. That proxy's public statement accepting a particular version permanently gives licensees the option to choose it for the Document. Acceptance neither compels migration nor extends the proxy's decision to every future version.
